They use sunlight, water and carbon dioxide (from air) to make food. This food making happens in the leaves, in a green pigment called chlorophyll. During this process, plants take in carbon dioxide and release oxygen into the air, which helps humans and animals to breathe.","concepts":[{"title":"What is Photosynthesis","summary":"Photosynthesis is the way green plants make their own food using sunlight, water, and air (carbon dioxide). This happens mainly in the leaves.","concept_key":"c5-science-photosynthesis-basics","scene_prompt":"A green plant in sunlight with its leaves facing the sky and roots in watered soil."},{"title":"Role of Chlorophyll","summary":"Chlorophyll is the green substance in leaves that helps plants trap sunlight and make food, and it gives leaves their green colour.","concept_key":"c5-science-chlorophyll","scene_prompt":"Sunlight shining on a bright green leaf showing its veins clearly."},{"title":"Gases Exchanged","summary":"During photosynthesis, plants take in carbon dioxide from the air and release oxygen, which is important for all living beings to breathe.","concept_key":"c5-science-gas-exchange-plants","scene_prompt":"A child breathing fresh air happily standing next to a leafy tree in a park."}]}
